title: AI-Driven Financial Inclusion with Enhanced Consumer Protection via Mobile Networks in Zambia
summary: Zamtel is piloting AI credit scoring and fraud detection over its mobile network; better access to loans, higher incomes and consumer protection remain intended benefits.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: Zamtel is piloting credit scoring and fraud detection that run over its mobile network. The project team states that "The aim is to enable over 500,000 unbanked Zambians to access micro-credit". Improved borrowing access, incomes and consumer protection remain intended benefits. The account reports no realized loan, income or fraud result.

data.answer:
Zamtel is piloting mobile-network credit scoring and fraud detection. Improved borrowing access, incomes, and consumer protection remain intended benefits.

The project is in progress, while the benefits section states income growth, fairness, and fraud protection as achieved properties without reported outcome data. Credit access alone does not establish improved welfare, and fair scoring requires subgroup error and lending-outcome analysis.

The project account does not separately evaluate AI’s contribution to the benefit.
